notes.text: The solitary place — Emmanuel's land, or the seat of God's church and people, which formerly was despised like a wilderness, and which the rage of their enemies had brought to desolation, shall flourish exceedingly.

The excellency — The wilderness shall be as pleasant and fruitful as Lebanon, and Carmel, and Sharon. They - The inhabitants of the wilderness aforesaid. The glory - The glorious discoveries of God's power and goodness.
Strengthen — Ye ministers of God, comfort and encourage God's people, who are now ready to faint.
Your God — Tho' he seems to be departed, he will come to you, and abide with you. He will shortly come in the flesh, to execute vengeance upon the enemies of God.
Then — The poor Gentiles, who before were blind and deaf, shall now have the eyes and ears of their minds opened to see God's works, and to hear and receive his word.

Streams — The most dry and barren places shall be made moist and fruitful; which is principally meant of the plentiful effusion of God's grace upon such persons and nations, as had been wholly destitute of it. Rushes - Those dry and parched deserts, in which dragons have their abode, shall yield abundance of grass, and reeds, and rushes, which grow only in moist ground.

A way — The high-way and the way are not to be taken for two different ways, but for one and the same way, even a causey, which is raised ground, and a way. Holiness - The people (walking in it) shall be all righteous. For those - But this way shall be appropriated to those persons above-mentioned; the weak, and blind, and lame, whom God will lead and save. Though fools - The way shall be so plain and strait, that even the most foolish travelers cannot easily mistake it. Sennacherib invades Judah, ver. 1. He sends Rabshakeh, who by his blasphemous persuasions tempts Hezekiah to despair, and the people to revolt, ver. 2-22. The history related here, and in the three following chapters, is, almost in the same words contained 2 Kings 18, 19, 20. It is inserted here, to explain and confirm some of the foregoing predictions. It may seem to have first been written by this prophet, and from him taken into the book of Kings, to compleat that history. Hezekiah mourns and sends to Isaiah to pray for them, ver. 1-5. He comforts them, ver. 6, 7. Sennacherib called away against the king of Ethiopia, sends a blasphemous letter to Hezekiah, ver. 8-13. His prayer, ver. 14-20. Isaiah's prophecy, ver. 21-35. An angel slays the Assyrians, ver. 36. Sennacherib is slain at Nineveh by his own sons, ver. 37, 38. Hezekiah in his sickness receives from Isaiah a message of death, ver. 1. By prayer, ver. 2, 3. hath his life lengthened; the sun goeth backward for a sign thereof, ver. 4-8. His song of praise to God, ver. 9-20.

glossa.text: *Shall rejoice.* The captivity of the Jews having been set forth, he treats of the conversion of the nations.
*Saron.* Of the people of the Jews; whence: *Saron shall be as a desert ((Isa. XXXII))*.

*The greenness of the reed.* The fulfilling of Scripture, which is signified by the reed; and the help of the intention, which by the rush: for the reed and the rush spring up and grow green beside the waters.

notes.text: For ever — Both because he liveth forever to fulfil his promises, and because he is eternally faithful. The psalmist praises God for his care over the church, ver. 1-14. His government over all, ver. 15-18. His giving his word to Israel, ver. 19, 20.

glossa.text: *Blessed is he whose God is the God of Jacob.* ((CAS.)) The third part, where he teaches that the whole hope is to be placed in the Almighty, whom he describes from his works, that the Gentile world, so often confuted, may be still. ((AUG.)) Hurtful things being removed, he teaches what belongs to salvation, namely, in whom hope is to be placed. *His helper is his hope.* ((CAS.)) Of that Jacob himself he was so the helper, etc., *as far as* that is, of this true Jacob, as of that one.

*Who made heaven and earth.* ((ID.)) Because the worshippers of demons also have hope in their god, he determines in whom hope ought to be, that is, in Christ, and this he shows even to the end of the psalm, describing him through all things. *All things that are in them.* Lest thou think any other to be the creator, or that there exists a creator even of the smallest things.

*Who keepeth truth for ever.* ((CAS.)) Christ, who is the truth; every man is a liar. *He executeth judgment.* These two pertain to justice. Christ the judge avenges those who suffer for his name, and gives food to them that love him. *For them that suffer wrong.* ((AUG.)) Not every trouble is a wrong. What thou sufferest by right is not a wrong, as is that which the robber and other wicked men suffer. It is one thing therefore to suffer wrong, another to suffer punishment. For a man suffers punishment by right, but wrong is contrary to right.

*The Lord looseth them that are fettered.* ((CAS.)) This belongs to the abundance of his sweetness.

*The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down.* Whom the devil casts down, the Lord lifts up.

*He loveth the just.* ((CAS.)) Whom he sets in eternal blessedness.

*The fatherless and the widow he will receive.* *suseipiet* ((AUG.)) The whole Church of the Gentiles is come as a stranger to the fathers, a daughter not by flesh but by imitation.

*The fatherless* are all who are in pilgrimage, whose father is absent; and every faithful soul is a *widow* while the bridegroom is absent: whence they desire the more both the father and the bridegroom, and God protects them, not seen but desired.

*The Lord shall reign for ever.* ((CAS.)) This is of his magnificence.

He shall reign in us when our hearts shall be firm in him, which is not yet.

notes.text: The husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit — Which will recompense his labour and patience. Till he receives the former rain - Immediately after sowing. And the latter - Before the harvest.
Stablish your hearts — In faith and patience. For the coming of the Lord - To destroy Jerusalem. Is nigh - And so is his last coming to the eye of a believer.
Murmur not one against another — Have patience also with each other. The judge standeth before the door - Hearing every word, marking every thought.

Take the prophets for an example — Once persecuted like you, even for speaking in the name of the Lord. The very men that gloried in having prophets yet could not bear their message: nor did either their holiness or their high commission screen them from suffering.

glossa.text: *Be patient ((ID.))* The proud and the unbelieving being rebuked, etc., *as far as* whence the Apostle: *You have your fruit in sanctification, and the end life everlasting ((Rom. VI))*.
*The prophets. ((ID.))* The prophets, who were so holy that the Spirit of God spoke his mysteries through them, etc., *as far as* concerning the Lord as regards the issue of death.

notes.text: He sent two of his disciples — Not because he doubted himself; but to confirm their faith. Luke vii, 18.
He that is to come — The Messiah.
Go and tell John the things that ye hear and see — Which are a stronger proof of my being the Messiah, than any bare assertion can be.
The poor have the Gospel preached to them — The greatest mercy of all. Isaiah xxix, 18; xxxv, 5.
Happy is he who shall not be offended at me — Notwithstanding all these proofs that I am the Messiah.

As they departed, he said concerning John — Of whom probably he would not have said so much when they were present. A reed shaken by the wind? - No; nothing could ever shake John in the testimony he gave to the truth. The expression is proverbial.
A man clothed in soft, delicate raiment — An effeminate courtier, accustomed to fawning and flattery? You may expect to find persons of such a character in palaces; not in a wilderness.
More than a prophet — For the prophets only pointed me out afar off; but John was my immediate forerunner.
Mal. iii, 1.

But he that is least in the kingdom of heaven, is greater than he — Which an ancient author explains thus: - "One perfect in the law, as John was, is inferior to one who is baptized into the death of Christ. For this is the kingdom of heaven, even to be buried with Christ, and to be raised up together with him. John was greater than all who had been then born of women, but he was cut off before the kingdom of heaven was given." [He seems to mean, that righteousness, peace, and joy, which constitute the present inward kingdom of heaven.] "He was blameless as to that righteousness which is by the law; but he fell short of those who are perfected by the spirit of life which is in Christ. Whosoever, therefore, is least in the kingdom of heaven, by Christian regeneration, is greater than any who has attained only the righteousness of the law, because the law maketh nothing perfect." It may farther mean, the least true Christian believer has a more perfect knowledge of Jesus Christ, of his redemption and kingdom, than John the Baptist had, who died before the full manifestation of the Gospel.

glossa.text: *Now John.* And while Christ was preaching, etc., *as far as* it does not appear who keeps the order of the thing done.

*Art thou he.* He does not say *who hast come,* as if he should say: Since I am about to descend to the lower regions: I ought to announce thee to those below, who have announced thee to those above. Is it fitting for the Son of God to die, or art thou about to send another for these sacraments ?
*He that shall not be scandalized.* He who shall not have doubted of the power of the divinity, he is not to be thought to have said this against John, whom he presently commends so greatly.

*Concerning John.* The forerunner of Christ wished to make his disciples certain concerning Christ, because he perceived that they doubted. Concerning the forerunner, Christ taught the doubting crowds not to doubt, since they thought him soft and light.

*Behold they who are clothed in soft garments,* etc. *Who put pillows under the elbow,* who soothe the life of sinners, and do not prick them.

A rigorous life and preaching ought to shun the palaces of the soft, which those frequent who flatter men clothed in soft garments.

((CLEM. ALEX.)) Blessed John, despising even the hairs of sheep, which savour of delicacies, [chose] the hairs of camels, etc., *as far as* he removed himself from all empty zeal, and from the vain appearance of good, and from a sordid and illiberal elegance.
*More than a prophet. ((BEDA.))* Because he is an angel not by nature but by office.

*Greater than John.* In this he is not preferred to the patriarchs and to all men, but is shown equal to the other saints. *But he that.* That is, every saint who is now with God is greater than he who is still in the world. Or I, whom the opinion of many makes less, am set before him in the Church of the saints. Or the last angel of heaven is better than any man whatever. *In the kingdom.* The kingdom of heaven is taken in two ways: either the one above, in which we are not yet: or the present Church, in which we still live, and already in a manner reign.

Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: that I will give the rain of your land in its season, the former rain and the latter rain, that you may gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
echoes.note: 'I will give the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain' is the covenant promise James invokes for the patient farmer who waits 'until it receives the early and late rain.' The early/late-rain pair is distinctive.

echoes.text: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.” In all this, Job did not sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
echoes.note: 'You have heard of the steadfastness of Job, and seen the outcome of the Lord' depends on the Job narrative — his endurance under loss without sin, and the restored 'outcome' of Job 42. James makes Job the type of patient endurance.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: 'How the Lord is full of compassion and mercy' reproduces the LORD's self-revelation, 'merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love' — the formula echoed across the Psalter (103:8; 111:4).

echoes.text: “Be glad then, you children of Zion, and rejoice in Yahweh, your God; for he gives you the former rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to come down for you, the former rain and the latter rain, as before.
echoes.note: 'He has given the early rain… the early and the latter rain' restates the same agricultural promise as a sign of restoration, reinforcing the patient-farmer figure.

echoes.text: Neither do they say in their heart, ‘Let us now fear Yahweh our God, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season; who preserves to us the appointed weeks of the harvest.’
echoes.note: 'Let us fear the LORD… who gives the rain in its season, the autumn and the spring rains' supplies a further early/late-rain antecedent.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
echoes.note: Jesus' catalog of signs answers John by weaving Isaiah's vision of the redeemed: 'the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped' — 'the blind receive sight, the deaf hear' borrows verbatim imagery, marking the dawning kingdom.

echoes.text: Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
echoes.note: 'Then shall the lame man leap as a hart' directly underlies 'the lame walk'; Isaiah 35 is the controlling subtext for Jesus' reply, signaling that the eschatological restoration has arrived.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: 'to preach good news to the poor' (anointed Servant) supplies the climactic 'the poor have good news preached to them' — the same verb/theme Jesus claims as his own programmatic mission (cf. Luke 4:18).
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind;

echoes.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.
echoes.note: 'the dead are raised up' echoes Isaiah's resurrection hope, 'Your dead shall live... the earth shall give birth to the dead,' folded into the kingdom-signs list.

echoes.text: In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of obscurity and out of darkness.
echoes.note: 'In that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see' — a parallel Isaianic oracle reinforcing the deaf/blind reversal, part of a recurring Isaianic cluster.

echoes.text: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: The Servant 'to open the blind eyes' resonates with restoring sight; strengthens the Servant-mission reading of Jesus' self-presentation.

echoes.text: “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
echoes.note: 'Hear, you deaf; and look, you blind, that you may see' — further Isaianic deaf/blind language drawn into the answer to John.

echoes.text: “This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. He shall be brought to the priest,
echoes.note: 'the lepers are cleansed' presumes the Torah cleansing rite for the healed leper; the only OT framework for leprosy cleansing, evoked figurally as fulfilled.

echoes.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
echoes.note: Naaman's cleansing is the paradigmatic prophetic leprosy healing; a faint precedent for 'lepers are cleansed' as a sign of prophetic power.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you' is a formula citation ('of whom it is written') of Mal 3:1, 'Behold, I send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me,' identifying John as the eschatological forerunner.

echoes.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: 'this is Elijah, who is to come' directly invokes Mal 4:5, 'I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD,' interpreting John as the returning Elijah.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
echoes.note: 'Behold, I send a messenger before you' (LXX wording 'before your face') is conflated with Mal 3:1 in the citation; the second-person 'before your face' tracks Exodus more closely than Malachi's 'before me.'

echoes.text: It was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entrance of the cave. Behold, a voice came to him, and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
echoes.note: The Elijah identification draws on the whole Elijah cycle; the wilderness/mantle prophet of austere dress stands behind the contrast with 'soft clothing' and the desert setting.

echoes.text: They answered him, “He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.” He said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”
echoes.note: Elijah 'a hairy man, with a leather belt' grounds the John-as-Elijah figure and the contrast with kingly 'soft clothing'; cf. Matthew's own description of John's garb.

echoes.text: The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of Yahweh in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.
echoes.note: 'What did you go out into the wilderness to see?' evokes the wilderness-voice preparing the way, the same way-preparation motif as the Mal 3:1 citation.

echoes.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
echoes.note: 'born of women' as a marker of mortal human descent is biblical idiom (cf. Job 14:1; 15:14; 25:4); the phrase frames John as the greatest of mortals.

echoes.text: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
echoes.note: 'Man who is born of a woman is of few days' supplies the idiom 'born of women' for finite humanity, against which John's greatness and the kingdom's superiority are measured.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The desert will blossom; the dry land will sing.
Sorrow and sighing will flee away.
The blind see, the lame leap, the silent shout.
This is the work of the One who comes.
Be patient, like the farmer waiting for rain.
The harvest of God is near.
Come, let us worship with joy.
Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the dry ground under your feet, cracked and thirsty — and then the water comes, and the desert breaks into bloom.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
The eyes of the blind are opening, the locked ears unsealed, the ones who could not walk are leaping like deer.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
So be patient, the way a farmer is patient, watching the sky for the early rain and the late.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come up the holy road with singing; the ransomed of the Lord are going home.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The thirsty desert blooms and starts to sing.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
The blind now see; the lame leap up for joy.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Be patient for the harvest, near at hand.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come, let us worship the God of joy.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.
